purpose: Track source-backed product workflows through discovery, independent wireframing, LDS implementation, and interaction verification without treating current screens or component files as coverage proof.
evidenceHierarchy: observed user actions in current source
UX audits and wireframe handoffs as problem signals
current product layouts and LDS components as non-authoritative candidates

stageDefinitions.discovered: The user goal, decisions, states, failures, recovery, and pinned source blobs are recorded.
stageDefinitions.wireframed: An independent low-fidelity workflow structure has been reviewed against every consumer source.
stageDefinitions.implemented: Minimal LDS components or composition contracts implement the reviewed wireframe without copying an application screen.
stageDefinitions.verified: Source requirements, wireframe, implementation stories, and interaction verification are traceably connected.

componentDisposition.name: SpeedDial
componentDisposition.reason: A bounded action-category component that does not own a product workflow or page layout.

componentDisposition.name: LogViewer
componentDisposition.reason: Owns log filtering, follow, and scroll behavior while the product retains transport and diagnosis.

componentDisposition.name: ReorderList
componentDisposition.reason: Owns only ordering of peer items and does not encode a procedure schema.

componentDisposition.name: Legend
componentDisposition.reason: Connects visual encodings to labels without owning the product renderer.

componentDisposition.name: LineChart
componentDisposition.reason: A bounded presentational chart whose data meaning remains application-owned.

componentDisposition.name: PropertyField
componentDisposition.reason: Can stay bounded to one field's current, draft, validation, and apply grammar.

componentDisposition.name: DockPanel
componentDisposition.reason: Owns dock, collapse, and resize layout behavior without imposing a product screen.

componentDisposition.name: DirectionalPad
componentDisposition.reason: A discrete momentary control input that remains separate from authority and transport.

componentDisposition.name: IconPicker
componentDisposition.reason: A standard single-value selection category independent of the audited product workflows.

componentDisposition.name: WheelPicker
componentDisposition.reason: A generic product picker that does not claim WDS date or time parity.

componentDisposition.name: FileUploadQueue
componentDisposition.reason: Owns per-file upload, processing, result, retry, and removal rather than the full operation workflow.

componentDisposition.name: SearchableMultiSelect
componentDisposition.reason: A standard asynchronous searchable multi-selection input.

componentDisposition.name: SecretField
componentDisposition.reason: Stays narrow to masked, reveal, and copy states without credential CRUD or publishing.

componentDisposition.name: EditorPanel
componentDisposition.reason: Fixes DockPanel, form, ActionArea, and dirty-close confirmation into a workflow shell without an independent interaction primitive.

componentDisposition.name: MetricComparison
componentDisposition.reason: A thin table wrapper that also derives product verdict policy; DataGrid or a product-owned table composition is sufficient.

componentDisposition.name: BatchOperationSummary
componentDisposition.reason: Fixes count, progress, failure rows, and retry actions into a product result block that existing status and action primitives can compose.

componentDisposition.name: SafetyConfirmDialog
componentDisposition.reason: A convenience wrapper around ConfirmDialog and Input; impact, blocker, and typed-phrase policy belongs to product composition.

componentDisposition.name: TerminalFrame
componentDisposition.reason: Only DeviceOps has an interactive terminal consumer; without its renderer and transport this is session-header and overlay composition.

componentDisposition.name: FileBrowser
componentDisposition.reason: Must be reduced to standard navigation and selection contracts instead of a compound product surface.

componentDisposition.name: TreeSelectionPanel
componentDisposition.reason: Must justify a persistent hierarchy-selection contract without duplicating Tree, checkbox, and search primitives.

componentDisposition.name: ExecutionStatus
componentDisposition.reason: Repackages product activity, outcome, freshness, and recovery into StatusBadge, ProgressBar, Timeline, and Callout layout.

componentDisposition.name: ReviewDecision
componentDisposition.reason: Owns draft choice, required reason, persistence state, and submit policy that the product should compose from ChoiceCard, Textarea, and ActionArea.

componentDisposition.name: TransitionGate
componentDisposition.reason: Gate evidence, state facts, notes, and actions are separate primitives; transition policy and persistence stay product-owned.

componentDisposition.name: CommandAction
componentDisposition.reason: A domain-specific wrapper around Button, ActionArea, and support text; eligibility and request errors are product state.

componentDisposition.name: CommandLifecycle
componentDisposition.reason: Repackages a product-owned phase schema into Timeline and status rows without adding an independent interaction contract.

componentDisposition.name: ConnectionStatus
componentDisposition.reason: Fixes ConnectionBadge, product-provided fact rows, and reconnect action into a status block; freshness, health, and recovery remain product policy.

componentDisposition.name: EvidenceViewer
componentDisposition.reason: Must narrow to image evidence rendering while provenance and availability chrome remain separate.

componentDisposition.name: ManualControlGuard
componentDisposition.reason: Must separate UI arming from control authority and contract safe release on blur, unmount, and link loss.

componentDisposition.name: TimeRuleEditor
componentDisposition.reason: Only one workflow currently consumes the once and weekly schema; compose shared form controls until an independent repeated contract is proven.

componentDisposition.name: DocumentSurface
componentDisposition.reason: Provenance and availability chrome, renderer slot, and patch decision are separate responsibilities.

componentDisposition.name: ScopedConversation
componentDisposition.reason: Source, scope, and reset use shared primitives while message rendering, draft, submit, streaming, and persistence stay product-owned.

componentDisposition.name: RunAction
componentDisposition.reason: Preflight evidence, admission or actual-run intent, and external-impact confirmation are distinct decisions.

componentDisposition.name: SchemaConfigEditor
componentDisposition.reason: The design system should supply change summary, dirty guard, and persistent actions instead of owning schema rendering.

componentDisposition.name: StepComposer
componentDisposition.reason: Ordering, validation summary, target summary, and the product-owned step editor are separate layers.

componentDisposition.name: ArtifactBrowser
componentDisposition.reason: Fixes an artifact table and detail-page structure that should be application composition.

componentDisposition.name: DatasetExplorer
componentDisposition.reason: Combines source rail, search, collection view, bulk actions, and pagination into a page-shaped component.

componentDisposition.name: LineageExplorer
componentDisposition.reason: Makes product graph meaning and layout a public design-system responsibility.

componentDisposition.name: AlertCollection
componentDisposition.reason: Encodes an alert inbox page instead of reusable collection and stable live-insertion behavior.

componentDisposition.name: ServiceControlRow
componentDisposition.reason: Hard-codes service statuses, actions, and confirmation into one domain-specific row.

componentDisposition.name: TopologyInspector
componentDisposition.reason: Fixes node, edge, layout, selection, and inspector responsibilities that belong to product renderers.

componentDisposition.name: ConversationMessages
componentDisposition.reason: Freezes a Context Hub message-array renderer as a public component although semantic list, error, retry, and source primitives are sufficient.

componentDisposition.name: ConversationComposer
componentDisposition.reason: A form, Textarea, and Button composition with product-specific draft and submit policy but no independent interaction contract.

componentDisposition.name: ApprovalTransition
componentDisposition.reason: Encodes one MLOps transition and derives submission eligibility from product-policy evidence inside the design system.

componentDisposition.name: PreflightSummary
componentDisposition.reason: Fixes outcome, check evidence, recovery, and recheck into a product workflow block that ValidationSummary, DescriptionList, and ActionArea can compose.

componentDisposition.name: ChangeSummary
componentDisposition.reason: Fixes current, proposed, validation, and impact fields into a read-only product schema that DescriptionList, DataGrid, and ValidationSummary can compose.

componentDisposition.name: CanvasEditorShell
componentDisposition.reason: Requires a separate audit against LDS siblings and official editor/accessibility references; pinned product sources may confirm workflow coverage only and do not decide anatomy, API, or style.

workflows.name: Attention to context
workflows.userGoal: Find the item that needs attention, open enough context to decide, and return without losing the investigation position.
workflows.trigger: The user enters an overview, queue, fleet, catalog, or project surface.
decisions: Which item needs attention first?
Is the current filter and freshness sufficient to trust the ranking?
Can the user return to the same query, page, selection, and scroll context?
failureRecovery: Distinguish no results from failed loading.
Keep query, filters, page, selection, and return context across detail navigation.
Do not reorder the user's reading position when live items arrive without an explicit reveal action.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own collection state, stable selection, attention markers, and return-context contracts; product ranking, queries, and routing remain application-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Should this remain a composition of collection primitives rather than a named domain explorer component?

workflows.name: Live truth investigation
workflows.userGoal: Separate current truth from stale cache and narrow a degraded entity to the evidence that explains it.
workflows.trigger: An entity appears offline, stale, degraded, anomalous, or inconsistent.

assetReviews.reason: Pinned supervision source confirms the need to summarize equipment identity, a primary condition, and supporting motion or connection facts. EquipmentStatusCard is independently designed from LDS Card/StatusBadge siblings and official status/summary-list references; Control retains telemetry truth, health diagnosis, recovery, and equipment-specific state machines, and its current ledger row, dimensions, and local prop names are not design authority.
Pinned map-editor source owns map and floor geometry authoring and does not consume a live equipment identity/condition summary.
Pinned assistant source owns project/evidence scope and conversation and has no physical-equipment identity, condition, or telemetry surface.

decisions: Is the displayed value current enough to act on?
Which evidence layer is the likely source: connection, input, processing, decision, service, facility, or event?
Is a write action safe while truth is uncertain?
failureRecovery: Project stale cached payloads as stale or offline instead of healthy.
Show the last trustworthy observation and its age.
Resynchronize after reconnection before re-enabling risky actions.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own freshness semantics, degraded presentation, evidence hierarchy, action gating, and an independently researched equipment identity/status/labeled-facts card; telemetry transport, domain diagnosis, recovery, and equipment-specific state machines remain product-owned. Product frontend anatomy, dimensions, styling, and local component APIs are coverage evidence only.
workflows.designQuestion: How should shared truth, equipment identity/status, and evidence priority work without imposing one dashboard or copied product-row layout?

workflows.name: Guarded remote action
workflows.userGoal: Understand whether a remote action is allowed, what it will affect, and whether the intended domain change actually happened.
workflows.trigger: The user requests a service, pipeline, board, robot, or task-changing command.
decisions: Why is the action enabled or blocked?
Is the impact reversible and does it affect an external system?
Did transport accept the command, did the target apply it, and was the resulting state independently confirmed?
failureRecovery: Keep failure, timeout, and late acknowledgement distinct.
Provide a safe retry only when idempotency and current truth allow it.
Retain command identity, actor, target, and result evidence.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own eligibility explanation, impact confirmation, lifecycle presentation, and retry affordance; authorization, command payload, idempotency, and confirmation watcher remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Which lifecycle surfaces must be separate components, and which belong only in product composition?

workflows.name: Staged change and apply
workflows.userGoal: Compare current and proposed values, resolve validation and impact, then know when the change is saved, applied, restarted, and verified.
workflows.trigger: The user creates or edits configuration, relationships, profiles, or execution parameters.
decisions: What changed from the current truth?
Which changes are live, restart-required, high-risk, or externally propagated?
Can the user safely leave, reset, save, apply, or restart?
failureRecovery: Keep field validation and server rejection at their owning scope.
Do not present saved as applied or verified.
Preserve the draft after a recoverable server error.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own dirty-state disclosure, change summary, validation hierarchy, impact labels, and sticky actions; schema, mutation, business validation, and restart policy remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Can a small change-summary and guarded-action set replace screen-sized schema and editor components?

workflows.name: Procedure authoring
workflows.userGoal: Turn an operational intent into an ordered, targeted, validated procedure that can be saved or explicitly submitted.
workflows.trigger: The user creates a task template or robot command sequence.
decisions: What outcome, robot, map, floor, landmark, or coordinate is the procedure targeting?
Is the order valid and what will each step do?
Should this remain a draft, be saved as a template, or be submitted now?
failureRecovery: Keep step-level validation attached to the step.
Distinguish saved template, submitted task, and active robot task.
Return from map picking without losing the editing position.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own ordered-item editing, step validation, and preview; command schema, map targeting, task payload, scheduling, and execution remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Which parts are reusable editing primitives, and which must remain a Control workflow instead of a StepComposer component?

workflows.name: Long-running operation
workflows.userGoal: Validate a costly operation, distinguish queueing from rejection, monitor honest result semantics, and decide how to recover.
workflows.trigger: The user requests training, evaluation, export, materialization, upload, conversion, or synchronization.
decisions: Did preflight validate only, or will the next action create an external effect?
Is the operation queued, rejected, or actively running?
What result scope was achieved and which artifacts or items failed?
failureRecovery: Keep partial success and item-level failure visible.
Explain retryability, cancellation, stale runtime, and required input changes.
Do not equate process success with external publish completion.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own preflight evidence, queued/running/result semantics, partial-result disclosure, and retry/cancel affordance; runners, uploads, conversions, slots, and side effects remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: How should one operation contract scale from a file queue to a long-running ML job without flattening their differences?

workflows.name: Human review decision
workflows.userGoal: Inspect evidence and persist an accountable accept, reject, or skip decision without treating review as an automated job.
workflows.trigger: A candidate, anomaly, or patch requires human judgment.
decisions: Is the evidence sufficient to decide?
Is a reason or note required?
Was the decision persisted before moving to the next candidate?
failureRecovery: Do not advance the queue until the decision is persisted.
Keep actor, timestamp, reason, and previous decision visible.
Keep incomplete or conflicting evidence visible instead of forcing a terminal review state.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own decision controls, required-reason states, progress, and actor evidence; decision policy, authorization, persistence, approval, and release truth remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Which small review controls are shared while evidence layout and approval transition remain separate?

workflows.name: Evidence and provenance investigation
workflows.userGoal: Trace a claim or anomaly to source evidence, relationships, freshness, and gaps before deciding.
workflows.trigger: The user opens logs, media, thermal evidence, pipeline relations, reports, dataset previews, artifacts, or citations.
decisions: What claim is this evidence supporting?
Where did it come from, when was it produced, and what is its authority?
What related evidence or missing gap changes the decision?
failureRecovery: Keep readable fallback or source representation when rendering fails.
Distinguish missing, unavailable, stale, and not-applicable evidence.
Preserve provenance and links when moving between graph, media, document, and artifact detail.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own evidence chrome, provenance metadata, fallback states, relationships, and accessible summaries; Markdown, graph layout, media decoding, overlays, logs, and artifact access remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Which evidence wrappers are truly shared, and which current viewers should be product renderers with LDS chrome?

workflows.name: Manual control safety session
workflows.userGoal: Acquire temporary control authority, move only while intent is continuously present, and stop safely on release or loss of truth.
workflows.trigger: The user opens direct robot, camera, gimbal, or jog control.
decisions: Is this the intended target and is live connection truth sufficient?
Does the user currently hold control authority and continuous intent?
What immediately stops motion on pointer, keyboard, focus, or connection loss?
failureRecovery: Send a safe stop on release, blur, unmount, and connection loss.
Keep emergency stop immediate and outside delayed confirmation.
Require deliberate re-arm after a safety release when policy requires it.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS Robotics may own focus, arm, hold/release, safety-release, speed-limit disclosure, and immediate e-stop affordance; command cadence, zero-velocity transport, robot protocol, and authority policy remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: What is the smallest safety wrapper that works with keyboard, joystick, D-pad, and PTZ controls?

workflows.name: Scoped knowledge assistance
workflows.userGoal: Ask within a known evidence scope, understand provider availability, and verify the sources used in the answer.
workflows.trigger: The user starts or resumes an evidence-backed assistant conversation.

assetReviews.reason: Pinned chat sources confirm the need for user/assistant turns, rich responses, loading/error handling, source links, and provider/project scope. LDS message, feed, composer, source, tree, and confirmation primitives cover those component types by composition; the product's current bubble geometry, color, citation disclosure, local prop names, transport, retrieval/RAG, persistence, participant-role truth, session policy, and citation truth are not LDS design authority.
Pinned map editor and task authoring sources own map and floor geometry plus task targets, with no evidence-backed conversation or citation entry point.
Pinned dashboard and task-command sources own supervision, task command, and manual-control workflows, with no scoped-knowledge conversation or citation UI.

decisions: Which provider and project scope are actually active?
Does changing scope invalidate the current session?
Which sources support the response and are they sufficient?
failureRecovery: Disable input when the provider is unavailable and explain why.
Explain whether the scoped conversation remains available after provider or scope changes; the product owns that session policy.
Keep failed input recoverable without inventing source truth; exact retry transport remains product-owned.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own independently researched document/bubble message anatomy, optional placement, controlled delivery/response lifecycle presentation, a named chrome-free log with history/follow behavior, a neutral elevated composer shell, generic attachment/source/action slots, active-scope disclosure, reset confirmation, and accessible streaming states. Participant-role truth, routes, provider transport, retrieval/RAG, scope resolution, persistence, session policy, and source truth remain product-owned. Pinned product UI is coverage evidence only and does not select LDS anatomy, geometry, color, tokens, props, or public component lifecycle.
workflows.designQuestion: Which general assistant conversation primitives are justified by LDS siblings, official AI-chat design-system references, and accessibility standards, and do the pinned products require those component types without defining their design?

workflows.name: Sensitive credential handling
workflows.userGoal: Use or update a secret with minimal disclosure and a clear audit boundary.
workflows.trigger: The user reveals, copies, creates, updates, or selects a credential.
decisions: Does the user need to reveal the secret, or can the product use a reference?
Is re-authentication or elevated permission required?
How will reveal, copy, update, and revoke be audited?
failureRecovery: Auto-hide revealed values and avoid exposing them in logs or generic props.
Keep the prior masked state when reveal or update fails.
Prefer passing a credential reference to downstream workflows instead of the raw value.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own masked/reveal/copy states and re-auth composition points; encryption, credential policy, permission checks, audit logging, and downstream use remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Can secret display remain a narrow field/action contract without absorbing credential CRUD or external publish?

workflows.name: External publish
workflows.userGoal: Validate an external target, make one explicit external-write decision, and prove what was actually published.
workflows.trigger: The user prepares a dataset, model, artifact, or release publish to an external system.
decisions: What target, path, privacy, and external write will occur?
Is this still validation-only or the actual publish?
What external evidence proves the publish and release scope?
failureRecovery: Keep validation-only and actual external write visually and semantically distinct.
Show partial or failed publish without presenting the release as complete.
Retain target, actor, attempt, and external evidence for retry decisions.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own external-impact disclosure, preflight evidence, explicit publish confirmation, and publish result presentation; target validation, credentials, upload, and external release truth remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Which confirmation and outcome pieces are reusable without making an MLOps publish screen component?

workflows.name: Schedule automation
workflows.userGoal: Bind an existing operation to a time rule, detect conflicts, and understand its future and current execution state.
workflows.trigger: The user schedules an operation or edits an existing schedule.
decisions: Which existing task, target, time zone, recurrence, and priority are being scheduled?
Does the rule conflict with another operation or an unavailable target?
Should an existing schedule be paused, resumed, changed, or deleted?
failureRecovery: Keep conflict details attached to the affected rule or target.
Distinguish schedule state from the state of an individual run.
Explain missed, failed, or expired occurrences without silently moving the next run.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own recurrence input, time-zone disclosure, conflict presentation, and schedule status actions; task lookup, conflict calculation, persistence, and run execution remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Which recurrence controls are generic while the schedule page and task semantics remain application-owned?

workflows.name: Approval transition
workflows.userGoal: Evaluate transition evidence, record the approving actor and note, and keep approval distinct from external release.
workflows.trigger: A version or release candidate requests a governed state transition.
decisions: Which transition is allowed by policy and what evidence is still missing?
What note and actor record are required?
Does the transition approve readiness or prove actual external release?
failureRecovery: Keep server rejection and missing gate evidence visible after submission.
Do not optimistically display the target state before persistence.
Keep approved and released separate until external evidence exists.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own evidence-gate presentation, required note, pending transition, actor history, and state distinction; transition policy, authorization, persistence, and release evidence remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Can approval use a narrow evidence-and-transition contract instead of sharing the review queue component?

workflows.name: Map navigation and facility authoring
workflows.userGoal: Inspect and edit map points, lines, regions, landmarks, and floor-specific task targets while preserving the semantic difference between elevator entry, elevator interior, door, waypoint, route, and region geometry.
workflows.trigger: The user opens a map editor or a floor-aware task authoring surface in LK Web Viz.

assetReviews.reason: Pinned map editor, zone editor, and task target sources map to renderer-neutral point, line, route, trajectory, region, facility-transition, and named-mirror contracts; projection, floor topology, editing, persistence, and recovery remain product-owned.

Pinned robot dashboard and task-command sources show a relevant supervision and map-target seam, but no component-level mapping to the six Robotics Navigation renderers has been closed; no support claim is made.
Pinned frontend evidence owns project and evidence scope, document intake, assistance, and credential workflows; it has no map, floor, robot-navigation, or geometry-authoring entry point.

decisions: Which map feature or facility endpoint is being inspected or edited?
Is the feature a point, line, region, landmark, or cross-floor facility relationship?
Which floor and map identity own the selected target?
Can the user distinguish the feature and its state at the current zoom without relying on color alone?
failureRecovery: Keep unsaved edits and the selected feature visible when save fails.
Distinguish missing map data from a loading or transport failure.
Do not collapse elevator entry, elevator interior, door, stair, and generic waypoint into one ambiguous marker.
Preserve a named list or inspector path when dense map geometry is not reliable for keyboard traversal.
workflows.dsBoundary: LDS may own renderer-neutral point, line, route, trajectory, region, facility-transition, selection, state, and accessible-mirror contracts; map persistence, editor commands, floor topology, task schema, facility control, and transport remain product-owned.
workflows.designQuestion: Do the navigation components and map symbols provide a coherent, conventional, zoom-stable visual grammar that LK Web Viz can compose without redrawing the same semantics?
